title: FDA De Novo review of Caption Guidance: nurses with no echo training acquire diagnostic heart ultrasound with AI guidance
summary: In FDA's review of Caption Guidance, eight nurses new to echocardiography scanned 240 patients with AI guidance; cardiologists judged left ventricular size assessable in 98.8% of exams.
account: Caption Health of Brisbane, California, makes Caption Guidance, software that coaches the user of an ultrasound probe toward standard views of the heart and records clips automatically. In the pivotal study, eight registered nurses with no echocardiography experience each scanned 30 patients at Northwestern Memorial Hospital in Chicago and Minneapolis Heart Institute between March and May 2019. A sonographer then scanned each patient without guidance. Five cardiologists judged the nurse exams to have sufficient quality to assess left ventricular size in 98.8% of exams, global left ventricular function in 98.8%, right ventricular size in 92.5% and nontrivial pericardial effusion in 98.8%. FDA granted the De Novo request on 7 February 2020. The study had no arm of nurses scanning without guidance, and two of the ten standard views reached diagnostic quality in fewer than 70% of exams.
purpose: Caption Guidance was built to help medical professionals, including those without echocardiography training, acquire standard cardiac ultrasound views. The measured benefit is that purpose.
developer: Caption Health, Inc. (listed as Bay Labs, Inc. in the FDA database)
deployer: Northwestern Memorial Hospital and Minneapolis Heart Institute
location: Chicago, Illinois, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States

ratings.reason: Nurses with no echocardiography experience produced exams that cardiologists judged sufficient to assess left ventricular size in 98.8% of patients.
FDA reviewers expect that patients would gain faster access to echocardiography, but the sources report no realized outcome for society beyond the two-site study.

ai_role.statement: The study compared guided nurse scans with unguided sonographer scans. It had no arm of nurses scanning without guidance, so the contribution of the software is not isolated.
